title: CS Quest 7.4 · Show and credit
name: Show and credit
summary: Teams finish the Credits and How-to in the question step (made by, idea from, art and sounds, thanks to our testers, how to play in three lines), then demo circles of six: a sixty-second demo that names one choice and why, then one question. The teacher visits each circle and marks the Explain & credit line on the lesson progress page.
iCan: explain one choice in my game in a sixty-second demo
write How to play in three lines a new player can follow
credit ideas, art and the people who helped
materials: Credits and How-to template printable (one per team)
demo card printable: who it is for, one choice and why, how to play (one per team)
the team folders with the captains' login cards
doNow: Who or what helped make your game? List everyone and everything, first names only.
plan: Arrive, captains log in, Do Now
Explore: a model demo and the credits template
Credits and How-to (8), then demo circles of six (10)

warmup.why: two retrieval items from the playtest, one vocabulary item, one preview of today, one more from the playtest

do: Give the model demo yourself with the frog quiz, sixty seconds by the clock: who it is for, one choice (the timer) and why, how to play in three lines. Then take one question from the class.

Put the credits template on the projector: Made by (first names or avatars) · Idea from · Art and sounds (the built-in art) · Thanks to our testers · How to play in three lines. Fill the first two lines for the frog quiz with the class.
say: A demo is not a speech about how great the game is. It names one choice and why you made it: we added a timer because our testers said it was too easy.
Credits are how you say who helped: the template you started from, the art you used, the ideas you borrowed, the testers who told you the truth. First names or avatars only.
ask: Your How to play is six lines long. Which three do you keep?
explore.afterAsk: Keep what the player does, how they win and one warning; cut the rest. Write the three lines on the board as the model.
explore.bigIdea: Explain one choice and why; credit everyone and everything that helped.

play.protocol: credits in the question step, then demo circles
creditsTemplate: Made by: first names or avatars
Idea from: a teammate, a classmate, a game you like
Art and sounds: the built-in art, anything a classmate drew for you
How to play, in three lines: what you do, how you win, one warning
demoCircles: Circles of six (three teams). Each team: sixty seconds of demo on its own device (who it is for, one choice and why, how to play), then sixty seconds for one question from the circle.
The listeners hold the demo card with the three things to listen for; the teacher visits each circle for one demo and marks the Explain & credit line on the lesson progress page afterwards.
lookFors: a demo that plays the game without talking: stop it and ask for the one choice
credits with a full name or a classmate's last name: first names or avatars only
a How to play longer than three lines
play.misconception: Kids think credits are only for things they copied; credits name everyone and everything that helped: the template, the art, the ideas, the testers, even a partner's note.
earlyFinishers: write What version 2 would have on the back of the demo card
listen to a second circle and write one question for a team there

discuss: What would version 2 have, and which tester or teammate gave you that idea?
Which choice in someone else's demo surprised you?
showMe: One team gives its sixty-second demo to the whole class on the projector; the class names the one choice it heard.

exit.sentencePrompt: Name one choice you are proud of and why you made it. Then write the first lines of your credits.
exit.frame: One choice I am proud of is ___ because ___. Credits: Art: ___. Idea: ___. Thanks to ___.

exit.paper: exit half-sheet (two per page) with the three items and the sentence frame

support: the demo card with three boxes to point at: who, one choice, how to play
the credits template with the lines pre-printed; the team fills the blanks
a quiet team demos to the teacher alone, then to one other team
stretch: add How it works: the main rule and the thing the player can see, in two lines
give the demo a second time to a different circle without the card

unpluggedTwin.title: Paper credits and demo circles
materials: each team's paper prototype or game
steps: Teams fill the credits template on paper: made by, idea from, art and sounds, thanks to our testers, how to play in three lines.
Circles of six: sixty seconds of demo with the paper prototype or the game, one choice and why, then one question.
The circle picks the demo that explained its choice best and says why.

subPlan: Do Now on paper, 3 minutes: who or what helped make your game; list everyone and everything, first names only.

Teams fill the paper credits template (made by, idea from, art and sounds, thanks to our testers, how to play in three lines), then demo circles of six: sixty seconds per team with the paper prototype or the game, one choice and why, then one question. No projector and no login needed; collect the templates for the teacher.
Paper exit ticket: the half-sheet with three questions and the sentence frame. Collect it.

steps.title: Today
steps.body:
Do Now: Who or what helped make your game? List everyone and everything, first names only.

Big idea: Explain one choice and why; credit everyone and everything that helped.

Today: finish your credits and How to play, then demo circles: sixty seconds, one choice and why, one question.

We will talk about:
- What would version 2 have?
- Which choice in someone else's demo surprised you?

steps.title: Warm-up (live)
steps.body: Five quick questions. Your teacher shows them on the projector or starts them live.

steps.title: Credits and How-to

levels: Nothing yet: no demo and no credits
Attempted: a demo or credits, but no choice is explained
Meets: the sixty-second demo names one choice and why, How to play is three lines, credits list the template, art, ideas and testers
Exceeds: the reason refers to the player's need, and a classmate could play from the How to play alone

steps.body:
Fill in every line. First names or avatars only, never full names.
- Made by: ___
- Idea from: ___ (a teammate, a classmate, a game you like)
- Art and sounds: ___ (the built-in art, anything a classmate drew for you)
- Thanks to our testers: ___
- How to play, in three lines: what you do, how you win, one warning.
- Our demo: the one choice we will explain, and why we made it.

steps.title: Exit ticket
steps.body: Three quick questions about demos, instructions and credits.
